Seminar Title:

Functional Mimicry of Solid Shortenings via Synergistic Polymer–Lipid Emulgels: Engineering Structure–Quality Relationships in Steamed Bread Formulations

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Speaker Type:

Abstract:

Traditional shortenings play a crucial role in stabilizing the gas cells, enhancing water-holding capacity, and modifying the crumb structure in bakery products. Hence, their substitution with alternative structuring agents is a daunting task. In this study, synergistic polymer-lipid emulgels made from cassia gum powder (CGP), psyllium husk polysaccharide (PHP), and rice bran oil (RBO) were designed as novel functional shortening mimics and applied to a steamed bread (SB) system. Various characterization techniques, including surface microscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), moisture analysis, and colorimetric studies, were employed to elucidate the effects of the emulgel compositions on the structure and quality attributes of the SB formulations. It was observed that replacement of in SB formulations with the polymer-lipid emulgels induced physicochemical modifications, especially the structural and quality attributes of these formulations, which were largely dependent on emulgel composition. Specifically, both too low and too high amounts of oil in the emulgel formulations drastically affected the crumb architecture. In this context, among the formulations, SB-CI2 (SB formulation prepared with 20% RBO) displayed an optimal structure-quality equilibrium, as evident from the consistent porous crumb structure, high moisture content, and desirable impedance profiles and color attributes. The balanced polymer-lipid network of SB-CI2 promoted the retention of gas, trapping water molecules, and formation of a coherent matrix, thereby facilitating the development of an organized crumb structure and improved quality characteristics. Notably, SB-CI2 could mimic the functionality of conventional shortenings while incorporating only a lower amount of actual oil, translating to 80% less oil incorporated into the SB matrix. These results revealed that these synergistic polymer-lipid emulgels could serve as tools for structuring quality attributes of SB formulations and as an alternative for developing healthier bakery products with lower oil content while keeping the structural attributes intact.
